title: Minimax rate of sequential binary calibration
formal: Determine \(C(T)=\inf _{A} \sup _{B} E[\sum _{p\in \mathrm{P}_{A}}|\sum _{t:p_{t}=p}(y_{t}- p)|]\) up to universal multiplicative constants as the integer horizon T tends to infinity, in the finite-forecast sequential game below. The requested rate includes logarithmic factors.
definitions: Before play, forecaster A selects a finite set \(\mathrm{P}_{A}\subseteq [0,1]\), which may depend on T. Both players know this set and T. At each time t, A selects \(p_{t}\in \mathrm{P}_{A}\) and adversary B selects \(y_{t}\in \{0,1\}\) simultaneously; neither sees the other’s current selection. Each may randomize using independent coins and the full history \((p_{s},y_{s})_{s<t}\), and after the round both selections become public. The infimum is over every such finite set and randomized forecaster, and the supremum is over all randomized adaptive adversaries. There is no computational restriction. The displayed sum measures unnormalized \(\ell\)\(_{1}\) calibration error and is finite; groups are defined by exact equality of predictions. Expectation is over both players’ coins.

context_blocks.text: Calibration asks whether forecasts agree with empirical frequencies on the rounds when each probability was announced. The minimax rate measures the unavoidable error in this requirement against an adaptive sequence of binary events.

The long-standing \(T^{2/3}\) upper bound has already been improved by a constant in the exponent. A lower bound strictly above \(\sqrt{T}\) is also known. Thus neither the old two-thirds barrier nor a square-root target is an appropriate new open question. The remaining problem is the optimal rate itself.

why: A fundamental quantitative problem in sequential prediction, with consequences for calibrated learning and decision making.
answer_criterion: Determine the stated minimax quantity up to universal multiplicative constants, including all logarithmic factors, with matching upper and lower bounds. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.

references.title: Breaking the \(T^{2/3}\) Barrier for Sequential Calibration
references.authors: Yuval Dagan; Constantinos Daskalakis; Maxwell Fishelson; Noah Golowich; Robert Kleinberg; Princewill Okoroafor

progress.text: The paper proves an upper bound \(O(T^{2/3- \varepsilon})\) for an absolute \(\varepsilon >0\) and a lower bound \(\Omega (T^{0.54389})\); these do not match.
